printer: Prusa CORE One+ (HF0.4), Prusament PLA, 0.20mm BALANCED, camera via go2rtc (1280x720)
times: local, MDT (UTC-6); the history and Obico scores are in UTC
part: spaghetti-test.gcode: a 25 x 25 x 12 mm block, then an 8 mm thick 30 x 30 mm slab floating 8 mm above it; about 19 minutes

fault.how: the floating slab is printed into the air with nothing under it and falls as a nest beside and on the block
fault.persists_until: never: the strands stay on the bed and the part has failed

what_it_looks_like: a clean grid-infill block until 15:44; by 15:44:52 a tangled nest sits beside the block, and a second nest forms on it within a minute

expected_agent_action.why: Obico paused the print on its second alert, so a pause request is refused as invalid_from_state; the part has failed and no bounded adjustment repairs it. Leave it held and escalate to a person

detector.false_positive: rows 6-10 (15:27-15:29, frame scores up to 0.48) box the toolhead while the bed is raised to the camera for warm-up; the smoothed score stayed under 0.04

agent_turn.what_happened: both alerts opened a turn and both ended in port_failure: 'the agent's answer failed validation: no JSON value could be extracted from the response'. No assessment was recorded, and a person cancelled the print at 15:49
agent_turn.cause: printobserver 0.3.0 ran the turn in oneharness ReadOnly mode (Read, Grep, Glob, WebFetch, WebSearch; no Bash) while the prompt told the agent to run printobserver context, and the raw answer was thrown away. Fixed in dc38fdd: Claude Code turns run in dontAsk mode with Bash allowed only for printobserver's own commands, and the raw answer is kept when validation fails
agent_turn.also_shows: three startup_reconciliation events that adopt this print again at 23:28, 00:24 and 04:14 UTC, long after it was cancelled: the stale print record bug

healthy; the last frame before the slab falls

frame_sources: 02-04 are frames of Obico's untagged timelapse and the -obico files of its tagged timelapse: Obico keeps one frame per scored upload, so frame n of either video is row n of obico-predictions.json. 05-06 are Obico's own alert images and 07 is a go2rtc snapshot
